Huron County Recorder
The County Recorder has the important and indispensable task of keeping the vital records pertaining to ownership in real estate (land) and to all encumbrances or liens upon it. Without the work of the County Recorder, it would be nearly impossible to purchase land and be assured of a clear title or to lend money with land as security.
Alert Me is a tool to notify you when a document containing your referenced name has been recorded in our office or has been recently corrected.
Notice of statewide recording fee changes due to legislative action
Effective January 1, 2025 the Huron County Recorder's Office will be charging the $5.00 document preservation surcharge for documents subject to the regular recording fees due to the enactment of SB 94. The new recording fee for the first two pages will be $39.00 (previously $34.00). Each additional page remains the same as current law at $8.00. Each marginal reference will continue to be $4.00.

Yesterday EVENT: Freeze Warning
ALERT:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 30 expected.
* WHERE...Portions of north central, northeast and northwest
Ohio and northwest Pennsylvania.
* WHEN...From 1 AM to 9 AM EDT Sunday.
* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions will kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
INSTRUCTIONS:
A Freeze Warning is issued when sub-freezing temperatures are
forecast to threaten outdoor plants. Those with agricultural
interests are advised to harvest or protect tender vegetation.
Potted plants outdoors should be covered or brought inside.
TARGET AREA: Lucas; Wood; Ottawa; Sandusky; Erie; Lorain; Cuyahoga; Geauga; Ashtabula Inland; Hancock; Seneca; Huron; Medina; Summit; Portage; Trumbull; Wyandot; Crawford; Richland; Ashland; Wayne; Stark; Mahoning; Marion; Morrow; Holmes; Knox; Southern Erie; Crawford

EVENT: Freeze Watch
ALERT:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 30 possible.
* WHERE...Portions of north central, northeast, and northwest Ohio
and northwest Pennsylvania.
* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Sunday morning.
* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
INSTRUCTIONS:
Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.
To prevent water pipes from freezing; wrap or drain or allow them to
drip slowly.

4 days ago 2:20pm - From the Norwalk Police Department :
Press Release 10/14/26
The Norwalk Police Department was notified by law enforcement authorities from Michigan they had received information that an individual that had commitment criminal acts in their jurisdiction was believed to be in the City of Norwalk. The individual was later located deceased of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound in field just north of the city limits. The local investigation has been turned over to the Huron County Sheriff’s Office. The Norwalk Police Department would like to thank the Bellevue Police Department, Huron and Erie County Sheriff’s Offices, the Norwalk Fire Department, North Central EMS, and the Huron County Prosecutor’s Office for their assistance.

2 weeks ago A friendly reminder that a burn ban is in effect.
The months of March, April, May, October and November favor the most for dry/dead vegetation. This combined with atmospheric conditions such as low humidity and breezy conditions create the environment for very fast spreading vegetation fires, which can easily threaten structures and other property. Stay safe everyone!

2 weeks ago Over the past couple of days, Director Mead and Deputy Director Stevens attended the 2026 Ohio Emergency Management Fall Conference for continuing education, training, and networking.
The conference brought together private sector, county, state, and federal professionals to share information and experiences on topics including mass casualty incidents, multi-agency response, emergency alerting, fire weather and wildfire impacts, environmental impacts, and more.
Opportunities like this help us stay prepared, strengthen partnerships, and better serve our community when emergencies happen.
